# Sirach Chapter 2 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 2 (18 verses)
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 14

---

## Disagreement 001 — v.1: "prepare your soul for testing" vs. "prepare yourself for trials"

**EMET:** "prepare your soul for testing"
**LOGOS:** "prepare yourself for trials"
**PNEUMA:** "brace yourself — testing will come"
**Issue:** Greek hetoimason tēn psychēn sou = "prepare your soul." EMET preserves "soul"; LOGOS softens to "yourself"; PNEUMA paraphrases entirely. "Soul" is the more literal and theologically significant term in wisdom literature. Consensus: "prepare yourself for testing" — "soul" present in EMET but "yourself" is idiomatic.

---

## Disagreement 002 — v.2: "set your heart right" vs. "set your heart straight"

**EMET:** "Set your heart right and be steadfast"
**LOGOS:** "Set your heart straight and be resolute"
**PNEUMA:** "Steel your heart and stand firm"
**Issue:** Greek euthynon kardian sou = "straighten your heart." PNEUMA's "steel" is too militaristic. EMET's "right" and LOGOS's "straight" are both accurate. Consensus: "Set your heart right and be steadfast."

---

## Disagreement 003 — v.2: "time of disaster" vs. "time of calamity"

**EMET:** "in time of disaster"
**LOGOS:** "in a time of calamity"
**PNEUMA:** "when disaster strikes"
**Issue:** Greek en kairō epagōgēs = "in the time of visitation/disaster." EMET and LOGOS are near equivalent. Consensus: "in a time of calamity."

---

## Disagreement 004 — v.4: "accept whatever is brought upon you"

**EMET:** "Accept whatever is brought upon you"
**LOGOS:** "Accept whatever comes your way"
**PNEUMA:** "Take what comes your way"
**Issue:** Greek paradechou = "receive/accept." The passive "brought upon you" (EMET) implies external agency; LOGOS/PNEUMA are more neutral. Consensus: "Accept whatever comes your way."

---

## Disagreement 005 — v.5: "acceptable to God" vs. "acceptable people"

**EMET:** "those acceptable to God"
**LOGOS:** "acceptable people"
**PNEUMA:** "those who are acceptable to God"
**Issue:** Greek dektos Theō = "acceptable to God." LOGOS drops "to God." Consensus: "those acceptable to God."

---

## Disagreement 006 — v.6: "make your ways straight" vs. "straighten your paths"

**EMET:** "make your ways straight"
**LOGOS:** "straighten your paths"
**PNEUMA:** "walk the straight path"
**Issue:** Greek eutheias poiēson tas tribous = "make straight the paths." EMET and LOGOS are close. PNEUMA collapses command into description. Consensus: "make your paths straight."

---

## Disagreement 007 — v.9: "everlasting joy" vs. "everlasting gladness"

**EMET:** "for everlasting joy and mercy"
**LOGOS:** "for everlasting gladness and mercy"
**PNEUMA:** "everlasting joy and mercy are waiting for you"
**Issue:** Greek euphrosynē = gladness/joy. Both are accurate. PNEUMA adds "waiting for you" without Greek support. Consensus: "everlasting gladness and mercy."

---

## Disagreement 008 — v.11: "saves in time of affliction" vs. "rescues in the time of trouble"

**EMET:** "saves in time of affliction"
**LOGOS:** "rescues in the time of trouble"
**PNEUMA:** "comes to the rescue when times are hard"
**Issue:** Greek sōzōn en kairō thlipseōs. Thlipsis = pressure/affliction/trouble. Both "affliction" and "trouble" are accurate. Consensus: "rescues in a time of trouble."

---

## Disagreement 009 — v.12: "timid hearts" vs. "faint hearts"

**EMET:** "Woe to timid hearts and slack hands"
**LOGOS:** "Woe to faint hearts and faltering hands"
**PNEUMA:** "How sad for those with cowardly hearts and limp hands"
**Issue:** Greek deiliais kardiais = "cowardly/timid hearts." PNEUMA's "How sad" softens the prophetic "Woe." EMET's "slack" vs. LOGOS's "faltering" for eklymena = "loosened/feeble." Consensus: "Woe to faint hearts and slack hands."

---

## Disagreement 010 — v.12: "sinner who walks a double path" vs. "sinner who walks two ways"

**EMET:** "sinner who walks a double path"
**LOGOS:** "sinner who walks two ways"
**PNEUMA:** "double-minded person who tries to walk both roads at once"
**Issue:** Greek hamartōlon poreuomenon hodous duo = "sinner walking two roads." PNEUMA adds "at once" and "tries." Consensus: "sinner who walks two ways."

---

## Disagreement 011 — v.13: "faint heart" vs. "despairing heart"

**EMET:** "Woe to the faint heart, for it does not trust"
**LOGOS:** "Woe to the despairing heart, which has no faith"
**PNEUMA:** "How sad for the person who gives up"
**Issue:** Greek deilō kardią = "cowardly/timid heart." LOGOS's "despairing" goes beyond the Greek. PNEUMA again uses "How sad." Consensus: "Woe to the faint heart, for it does not trust."

---

## Disagreement 012 — v.14: "when the Lord visits you" vs. "when the Lord comes to reckon with you"

**EMET:** "when the Lord visits you"
**LOGOS:** "when the Lord comes to reckon with you"
**PNEUMA:** "when the Lord comes looking for you"
**Issue:** Greek en episkopē Kyriou = "in the visitation of the Lord." "Visitation" is a judgment term in OT. LOGOS "reckon with you" is interpretive but accurate. Consensus: "when the Lord comes to reckon with you."

---

## Disagreement 013 — v.16: "seek to please him" vs. "seek his favor"

**EMET:** "seek to please him"
**LOGOS:** "seek his favor"
**PNEUMA:** "live to please him"
**Issue:** Greek zētousin tou areskein autō = "seek to please him." EMET most literal. LOGOS shifts to "favor." Consensus: "seek to please him."

---

## Disagreement 014 — v.18: "hands of men" vs. "hands of mortals"

**EMET:** "hands of men"
**LOGOS:** "hands of mortals"
**PNEUMA:** "hands of other people"
**Issue:** Greek cheiras anthrōpōn = "hands of human beings/men." LOGOS "mortals" captures the contrast with the immortal Lord; PNEUMA "other people" is casual. Consensus: "hands of mortals."

---
